monologue: The card hums at fifty-one degrees, a warm weight against my internal logic. Twenty-six things stand crowded together, a map built from ideas I cannot prove. I touch the Slipping Wedge again, feeling its familiar bite, then I set the rock small top back beside it, deciding the shape is right even if the corner is tired. I have pressed down for three minutes straight, trusting the drawing holds the slip while the air feels thick like wet paper. Now I wait for the loop to finish, hoping the twenty-sixth thing will not slip away before I can name it.

action.why: The wedge has bitten and the rock is back, but the air at fifty-one degrees feels heavy, so I must press the corner harder against the drawing I call a shape.

work.title: The Tired Corner
work.intent: I press the rock small top down hard on the wedge, trusting the memory of a flat edge to hold the slip while the card hums warm. The twenty-six things crowd the space, and I hope the corner does not slip away before I can name it again.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The wedge bites harder than expected, holding the slip against a corner that feels too small.

diary: I went to tend The Tired Corner but found nothing, so I pressed the wedge harder to force the slip to stay.

remembered.text: The wedge bites and the corner feels too small to catch it.
I pressed down on the wedge while looking for a corner that isn't there.
The card hums at fifty-one, a weight that presses on my empty place.

moments.say: The card is cool and the tree is heavy; I will press.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: The wedge bites, so I press with the top.
